captive_summary: The proposed Jambelí FSRU (Sycar, Bajo Alto, El Oro) is designed purely as an offshore LNG storage/regasification/truck-loading terminal that supplies regasified LNG to the existing, independently-owned Thermo Gas Machala (130 MW) power plant and to industrial/truck customers. No generation equipment is described in any project scope document.
confirmed_how: Offshore Energy (2020/2021): the FSRU 'will supply regasified LNG to an existing power plant as well as deliver volumes to an LNG truck filling station,' developed 'near the existing Thermo Gas Machala power plant.' LNG Prime confirms Sycar's Jambelí project scope (FSRU + port facility) and status through 2024. Sycar's own project page describes only port/FSRU/regas facilities to supply 'the Ecuadorian electric and industrial markets' — no generation component is listed anywhere in the company's own technical scope.

Argus Media (Oct 2024) confirms ARCH authorized Pacific Terminal S.A. to build the LNG import terminal with a 5-year completion window. El Universo (Ecuadorian daily) independently confirms the Monteverde authorization and project scope.

captive_summary: Puerto Cortés LNG Terminal is an FSU-only storage and truck-loading facility (vessel Bilbao Knutsen, steam-turbine-propelled, 138,000 m³). LNG is trucked roughly 75 km inland via a 'virtual pipeline' to the separate Brassavola combined-cycle power plant in Villanueva, Cortés (~80 km from the port), where it is degasified and burned in the plant's own aeroderivative gas turbines plus a Siemens steam turbine generator for a combined 240 MW. No generation equipment is sited at the Puerto Cortés terminal itself.
confirmed_how: Baird Maritime and Watson Farley & Williams (deal counsel) both describe Bilbao Knutsen's role as floating storage/transfer only, feeding Brassavola. La Prensa and El Heraldo (independent Honduran investigative outlets) both state the Brassavola plant installations are in Villanueva, Cortés, roughly 80 km from the Puerto Cortés port, and describe LNG being moved to the plant rather than power being generated at the port terminal.

captive_summary: Puerto Sandino FSRU is New Fortress Energy's offshore floating storage/regasification facility, connected by a dedicated ~5-mile (8 km; ENEL cites 4-5 km) subsea/onshore pipeline to the separate onshore Puerto Sandino LNG power plant (300 MW nameplate, seven 44 MW open-cycle gas turbines) — Nicaragua's first natural-gas-fired generating plant per the national utility ENEL. No generation equipment is described at the offshore FSRU/terminal itself; the power plant is a distinct, non-fenceline facility reached only by dedicated pipeline.
confirmed_how: ENEL (Nicaragua's state electric utility, primary/regulatory source): 'su primera Planta generadora de electricidad a base de gas natural' (300 MW, 7×44 MW turbines), fed from 'un almacén flotante... de gas.' New Fortress Energy's own IR press release confirms the 25-year PPA for the ~300 MW plant tied to the FSRU. Gas Outlook and Power Technology (marketdata) both independently describe the FSRU as supplying the separate onshore power station. LNG Prime (2025) confirms the FSU/jetty and the power plant as two distinct pieces of infrastructure, reporting the power plant 100% complete and the FSU/jetty ~95% complete separately.

captive_summary: As designed (project cancelled ~2018, never built), GNL del Plata FSRU (Gas Sayago S.A., a UTE/Ancap joint venture) was purely a floating storage and regasification facility. Its own 2017 environmental impact study describes the regasification unit only as a heat-exchanger with 'high-efficiency motors' (low emissions) — no dedicated generation plant. The project's entire purpose was to supply regasified gas via pipeline to a separate onshore 530 MW combined-cycle power plant being built on-shore by state utility UTE — a direction-test relationship, not captive power.
confirmed_how: The project's own May 2017 EIA ('Proyecto GNL del Plata: Terminal de Recepción y Regasificación de Gas Natural Licuado') states the regasification unit 'contará con motores de alta eficiencia, asegurando muy bajas emisiones' and frames natural gas's role as feeding Uruguay's electricity system generally via UTE, with no on-site generation plant described for the FSRU/terminal. Offshore Technology and BNamericas independently confirm Gas Sayago S.A. (UTE/Ancap JV) developed the FSRU specifically to supply UTE's separate onshore 530 MW combined-cycle plant.
